1.
Learned A.G.A. informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter including up-to-date case diary and charge sheet in this case has also been submitted.

2. Perusal of the record would reveal that vide communication of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Unnao dated 01.08.2023, the service on opposite party No.2 is shown to be sufficient however, no body is present on her behalf.

3. Heard Shri Arunendra Nath Mishra, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
4.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Shivkumar @ Shiva for grant of bail, in Case Crime No.29 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. & 5(J)(ii)/6 POCSO Act,
Police Station Makhi, District Unnao, during trial.

5. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.
Applicant has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecutrix.

6. It is further submitted that first information report of this case has been lodged by the mother of the victim/prosecutrix on 07.02.2023 pertaining to an incident which had taken place on 18.12.2022 stating therein that her daughter aged about 16 years had fled away from her home on 18.12.2022 however, after many months of fleeing away from her house, the prosecutrix was recovered and her statement under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded wherein she has clearly stated that she had accompanied the applicant with her free wish and will and she was not enticed away and they had solemnized marriage in Meerut.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she maintained that the applicant had not committed anything wrong with her.

7. It is vehemently submitted that the age of the prosecutrix determined through the ossification test is 19 years while as per her educational credentials, her age is coming about 17 years 7 months and 8 days on the date and time of incident and even if she was not major but was having sufficient intellect to understand her welfare and as she had gone with the applicant with her free will, wish and consent, no offence in fact has been committed by the applicant moreso when no abnormality has been found in the medical examination report of the prosecutrix.
8. It is next submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 18.02.2023.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
9. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

10. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the age of the prosecutrix determined through the ossification test is 19 years on the date of incident,
while as per the educational credentials, her age appears to be 17 years and 7 months.
No source has been disclosed in the school record on the basis of which the age of the prosecutrix had been recorded therein.
Thus, the educational age of the prosecutrix may not be taken as conclusive and the same is yet to be determined by the trial court after providing an opportunity to lead evidence to the parties.

The prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. categorically stated to have accompanied the applicant with her free will and consent and also that they had solemnized marriage at Meerut.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she maintained that the applicant had not committed anything wrong with her.
Applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 18.02.2023 without any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in this case has also been filed and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

11. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

12. Let the accused/applicant- Shivkumar @ Shiva involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
( i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
13. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
14. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
15. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.

Order Date :- 18.8.2023 Saurabh Yadav/-
